findings.title: totalPages counts one page too many when user_count is an exact multiple of limit.
findings.body: `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` gives 2 pages for 50 members with limit 50, and 3 for 100. `showingLast` stays false on the real last page, so the user can click Next to an empty page (offset 50 of 50) showing "2/2". The same thing happens after removing a member brings the count down to a multiple of the limit. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

findings.title: The public members endpoint takes limit and offset from the client without bounds.
findings.body: `limit` and `offset` come straight from params. A negative value (e.g. `offset=-1`) makes Postgres reject the query, which gives a 500. `limit=0` is echoed back in `meta.limit`, and the client stores it and divides by it in `currentPage`, `totalPages` and `next`, so the page counts become NaN or Infinity. A very large limit lets any viewer of a group load all of its members in one request. Clamp both values, e.g. `limit = [[limit, 1].max, 200].min` and `offset = [offset, 0].max`.

findings.title: Add/remove member requests have no error handler, so failures are silently ignored
findings.body: `removeMember` and `addMembers` only add a success callback, and the controller actions that call them (`removeMember` and `addMembers` in admin-group.js.es6) ignore the returned promise. If a request fails, for example with a 422 for an automatic group, an unknown group or a server error, the admin gets no message and the member list is not reloaded, so the UI looks as if the action may have worked. Fix: add a rejection handler that shows `e.responseText` errors with `bootbox.alert`, as `save` does, and reload the list in both cases.

findings.title: The public group members page now shows only the first 50 members and has no way to page.
findings.body: The server now returns 50 members by default for every group. Before, non-automatic groups returned all their members. The public `group/members` template only loops over `members` and has no next/previous controls, and its route never changes the offset. So any group with more than 50 members now shows a silently truncated list on the public page. Add paging controls to this page, or keep loading the full list here.

findings.title: Adding a user who is already a member returns a 500 error.
findings.body: `add_members` calls `group.add(user)` for every username without checking whether the user is already in the group. If `Group#add` pushes onto `users`, as it does in Discourse, the unique group_users index raises and the request returns a 500. This is easy to hit because the admin UI never clears the username input after a successful add (see the TODO), so clicking Add a second time sends the same usernames again. Skip users who are already members, e.g. `group.add(user) unless group.users.include?(user)`, or check with an exists query.

findings.title: Overlapping findMembers responses can leave the wrong page displayed
findings.body: `findMembers` writes `offset`, `limit`, `user_count` and `members` onto the shared Group model from whichever response arrives last. `next` and `previous` change `offset` and send a new request right away, and nothing cancels or ignores the earlier request. If an admin clicks quickly, or an add/remove reload overlaps a page change, an older response can arrive last and overwrite the newer state, so the members shown do not match the page counter the user expects. Fix: keep a request counter and ignore any response that is not from the latest request.

findings.title: The automatic-group test for remove_member sends PUT, but the route only accepts DELETE.
findings.body: In `config/routes.rb`, `remove_member` is mapped only to `delete "members"`, and the sibling test "is able to remove a member" uses `xhr :delete`. This test looks copied from the `add_members` case and still sends `:put`. Controller specs call the action directly, so the test can pass with a verb the real route rejects. It therefore doesn't check the request a client would actually send. Use `xhr :delete` so it matches the route and the sibling test.

held.title: Removing a member with users.delete skips GroupUser callbacks and raises an error for non-members.
held.body: `group.users.delete(user_id)` on a has_many :through deletes the join row directly, so GroupUser destroy callbacks (such as clearing the user's primary group or title) and the cleanup in `Group#remove` don't run. I couldn't check here what those callbacks do. Also, when the id is not a member, `delete` looks up the record and raises RecordNotFound, which turns into a 404 instead of the silent success the old code gave. Use `group.remove(user)` with `User.find(user_id)`, as the old code did.
